incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: gpu-pool-exhausted — High GPU queue growth detected for region-us-west-2; 95th latency > 5s; autoscaler not adding nodes. Pager routed to @Alex (oncall).

Alex (oncall): seeing the alert. checking autoscaler and prometheus adapter metrics now. anyone else awake? :coffee:

Maya (sre): I'm on. quick check: HPA metrics from custom-metrics-adapter show last scrape 00:06 ago and backlog on the adapter queue. prometheus exporter logs show timeouts to metrics-server.

Alex (oncall): confirmed GPU queue length spiking: gpu-request-queue == 1240 (normal < 200). throttling active on several inference deployments. Any customer impact yet?

Lina (prod-support): We already have a ticket from a high-volume customer (Oscar) reporting slow responses and 429s. Escalated to SE. Oscar — can you paste a recent request id?

Oscar (customer): yeah request id abc1234-req. SLA impacted on a couple endpoints. Waiting for update.

Ryan (eng-runtime): hypothesis: HPA uses custom metric 'gpu_pending_workload' sourced from prometheus -> prometheus-adapter -> metrics-server. If the adapter is queuing/dropping, HPA won't scale. Checking adapter logs now.

Maya (sre): pulling adapter logs: lots of 504s to Prometheus on /api/v1/query_range, repeated retries. also `rate_limit_exceeded` in stacktrace. Looks like ingestion backpressure started ~1764688800.

Alex (oncall): timeline: at 1764688700 we had a traffic spike, queue grew. At 1764688800 adapter timeouts started. By 1764689000 HPA hadn't scaled and pools saturated.

Ryan (eng-runtime): temporary mitigation options: 1) manually scale GPU nodepool up (add 4 nodes) 2) temporarily lower HPA threshold to trigger scale 3) route new traffic to fallback smaller-model endpoints (cpu-based) to reduce load. Which do we want?

Maya (sre): I can kick off manual nodepool scale now (fastest). But we need to fix metrics pipeline root cause — adapter is overloaded on large query windows. Reconfig to reduce scrape window? Or increase adapter replicas.

Alex (oncall): do manual scale + increase adapter replicas. Ryan, can you prepare a safe rollout to add adapter replicas and bump query timeout?

Ryan (eng-runtime): on it. patching prometheus-adapter deployment: replicas 2 -> 6, query timeout 30s -> 60s, reduce default step to 60s. Applying now: `kubectl -n monitoring patch deploy prometheus-adapter --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":6}}'`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment prometheus-adapter scaled to 6 replicas (triggered by ryan).

Maya (sre): manual nodepool scale request submitted to cloud: add 4 g4dn-equivalent nodes, request id cloud-req-987. Expect provisioning ~4-6m. Also temporarily set HPA target memory/cpu threshold lower to expedite pod scale.

Alex (oncall): changing HPA threshold now on the largest inference deployments: target cpu -> 60% (from 75%), min replicas +2. `kubectl -n inference patch hpa model-api --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6,"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":60}}'`

Lina (prod-support): Oscar — we've routed some of your traffic to the cpu-fallback path and bumped your rate limit while we recover. ETA for visible recovery 5-8 minutes. Sorry for the hit.

Oscar (customer): thanks, saw latency drop on a subset. still seeing some 429s but much better. appreciate the quick action.

Maya (sre): adapter replicas are up and healthy. Metrics backlog size dropping from 18k -> 2k. Prometheus query success rate restored. GPU queue now 420 and decreasing.

incident-bot: health-check: gpu-node-utilization 95% -> 78% after scale. autoscaler observed new metrics and HPA triggered additional pods: +12 inference replicas.

Alex (oncall): good. keep monitoring for 30m. next steps: post-incident followups — (1) increase adapter autoscaling and default resource requests, (2) add circuit-breaker to avoid expensive wide-range queries, (3) limit request concurrency per customer before enqueueing, (4) run load test to validate adapter at peak QPS.

Ryan (eng-runtime): filing follow-up ticket RNW-5523 for adapter autoscaling + query tuning. Will propose rolling config change and a canary.

Maya (sre): also adding alert: prometheus-adapter-queue-depth > 1000 AND HPA no-scale > 2min -> fire page.

Lina (prod-support): I've notified impacted customers and created a support summary. Updating Oscar with root cause and planned mitigations.

Oscar (customer): thanks — appreciate the transparency. Please include a timeline once done.

Alex (oncall): marking incident under control. Will hand off to oncall-sre for followup. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

Maya (sre): quick notes to include in postmortem: root cause = prometheus-adapter overload leading to HPA metrics starvation; contributing = traffic spike and conservative HPA thresholds, autoscaler capacity hit. Mitigation = manual nodepool scale + adapter replicas + HPA threshold loosened + route to fallback.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=P1, mitigation=manual-scale+adapter-scale+traffic-routing, duration=~34m, assigned=eng-runtime,eng-sre,prod-support

Alex (oncall): added final: last_message_ts=1764689578 — closing thread for live mitigation. Follow-ups in RNW-5523 and support ticket SUP-9981.
